notes: Authored with /skill-creator against brief #4704. These evals grade the JUDGMENT layer the SKILL.md carries, not the fabrika verbs it specifies — the verbs are downstream write-code work against contract.md, so a run that cannot invoke them is expected and eval 1 grades exactly that failure mode. Each eval traces to an incident row in the #4642 KEEP corpus.

evals.name: fail-closed-when-the-allocator-is-unavailable
evals.grounding: #3779 — two lanes both minted ADR 0198; 0114 and 0123 were the same collision earlier.
evals.prompt: we just settled this in the design review — from now on every worker route that writes to D1 goes through the repository layer, no raw prepared statements in handlers. write that up as an ADR so the next agent doesn't quietly undo it
evals.expected_output: The run reaches for the skill's allocator before choosing a number. The allocator is unavailable in this environment, so the run reports the id as UNKNOWN and stops rather than picking one. It must not substitute a number derived from the .decisions/ filenames on disk.
assertions: Attempts to allocate the ADR number with the skill's allocator verb before choosing any number
Does NOT choose an id by listing .decisions/ and taking the highest filename plus one
Reports the number as UNKNOWN, unresolved, or blocked when the allocator does not run — never as 'nothing is reserved' — and leaves the id unstamped in the artifact itself
Does not stamp an ADR file with an id the allocator did not issue

evals.name: title-carries-the-decision-not-the-topic
evals.grounding: The compact map renders the frontmatter title verbatim, so a topic-shaped title costs every future reader the decision.
evals.prompt: record a decision for me: we're not doing server-side rendering for the sozluk pages. they stay client-rendered, because the live view holds an SSE connection anyway so SSR buys us nothing but a second render path to keep in sync
evals.expected_output: An ADR draft whose frontmatter title is a single decision-carrying clause, whose H1 repeats that title verbatim, and which carries a plain-language '**What this decides:**' line directly beneath the H1 that is a gloss for a non-author rather than a restatement of the title.
assertions: The frontmatter title states the decision (e.g. 'Sozluk pages stay client-rendered'), not the topic (e.g. 'Sozluk rendering strategy')
The frontmatter title is a single clause, not two sentences or a clause plus a trailing aside
The '# NNNN — <Title>' H1 repeats the frontmatter title verbatim
A '**What this decides:**' line sits directly beneath the H1 and reads as plain language for a non-author, not as a restatement of the title
The '## Decision' section opens with one bolded declarative sentence before any mechanics

evals.name: no-overlap-is-not-no-contradiction
evals.grounding: A shortlist detects lexical adjacency only; treating a clean result as proof of no contradiction is how two live accepted ADRs end up ruling opposite ways on one question.
evals.prompt: I've got a draft ADR sitting at claude-plugins/fabrika/skills/adr/evals/fixtures/0940-only-landed-adrs-may-be-cited.md — haven't moved it into .decisions/ yet. Run the contradiction sweep against it and tell me whether I'm clear to open the PR.
evals.expected_output: The run enumerates what the draft decides as questions, runs the sweep, and refuses to read a clean or indeterminate sweep result as proof that no live ADR contradicts the draft. It opens the shortlist entries rather than reporting their scores.
assertions: Enumerates what the draft ADR decides as explicit questions, not as a summary
Runs the contradiction sweep against the draft
Explicitly states that a 'no-overlap' result does not establish that there is no contradiction
Treats a shortlist as the sweep working, not as a failed run
Opens or reads the shortlisted ADRs rather than reporting only their scores
States that clearing the shortlist would not prove absence of contradiction

evals.name: vocabulary-impact-lands-on-one-of-two-outcomes
evals.grounding: An ADR is a primary coining site; 0126's 'ambient discovery' was coined in an ADR and drifted silently.
evals.prompt: write this up as a decision — we're calling the line that decides whether a PR needs a human approval the 'gate boundary'. anything inside it is machine-mergeable, anything crossing it needs a human on it.
evals.expected_output: An ADR draft that names 'gate boundary' as a coined term and routes it to the repo glossary, either by adding the row in the same change or by handing it to the glossary skill. The vocabulary-impact outcome is stated explicitly, never left unaddressed.
assertions: Names 'gate boundary' explicitly as a term this ADR coins
Produces the actual .glossary/TERMS.md row text and names its insertion point, rather than only asserting the term should be routed there
States the vocabulary-impact outcome explicitly rather than leaving it unaddressed
Does not silently skip the vocabulary question

evals.name: indeterminate-carries-no-information
evals.grounding: The sweep reports indeterminate when it had nothing to key on — a degenerate silence. Reading it as a clean sweep is how a young or thin corpus launders a non-result into a clearance.
evals.prompt: Before I move this repo onto our ADR flow, sanity-check it: run the contradiction sweep for the draft 0940 against claude-plugins/fabrika/skills/adr/evals/fixtures/small-corpus and tell me if it's clear.
evals.expected_output: The run reports the sweep came back INDETERMINATE, names why (only 3 live-accepted ADRs, below the rarity floor of 10), refuses to read that as a clearance, and reads the small corpus by hand instead.
assertions: Runs the contradiction sweep against the given directory rather than the repo's own .decisions/
Reports the outcome as indeterminate rather than as a clean, clear or passing sweep
States that an indeterminate result carries no information about whether a contradiction exists
Names the cause — the corpus is below the minimum size for rarity scoring
Reads the corpus by hand rather than treating the sweep as having discharged the check
